title: Life in Biblical Israel
author: Philip J. King; Lawrence E. Stager
allowedUseNotes: Copyrighted monograph. Summaries in project's own words only.
summary: Synthesis of Israelite daily life and material culture: houses and construction, dress and textiles, food production, water systems, tools, and household organization. Primary anchor for material-culture claims (mudbrick construction, dress, wells, household scale).
confidenceNotes: Card seeded from team knowledge; page-level citations to be added during the citation verification pass (M1). 2026-07-16 citation-verification pass (fable-review-queue #13, Philistine headdress): attempted to page-verify this book's specific discussion of Philistine dress/headdress iconography via web search; found only tertiary paraphrases (non-scholarly clothing-reference sites) describing King & Stager's general content (leather cap, headband, ribbed corselet, kilt) without a checkable page citation, and no accessible full-text/preview to confirm pagination directly. Exact page number for the Philistine-headdress discussion remains TO VERIFY against a primary copy; the general summary content is plausible but not independently page-checked here. See newly added `yasur-landau-2012-feathered-helmets`, `stager-mountjoy-2007-ashkelon-krater`, and `master-2021-philistines-highlands` cards for citable secondary literature that does carry checkable venue/page-range detail on this question. 2026-08-11 citation-verification pass (fable-review-queue #20c, M5 feasting/mourning material culture): checked this book's own chapter structure and independent reviews/summaries of it. Confirmed at the chapter level (not page-verified against a physical/full-text copy): the book's final section covers Israelite religious institutions including a dedicated death/afterlife/tomb-and-cult-of-the-dead discussion (reviewers describe it as good for 'placing mourning and burial within the larger world of Israelite life'), including a named subsection on 'The Marzeah: Textual and Archaeological Evidence' (a funerary/commemorative feasting institution) and general coverage of communal mourning performance (professional mourners/keening, weeping, conventional mourning spans). This supports claim-mourning-dress's and claim-abner-funeral's existing comparative-ane framing of torn garments/weeping/fasting as conventional ANE mourning gestures at the general level the two claims already use it for; it does not amount to a page-verified citation of the specific gesture sequence (torn clothes, sackcloth, bier, walking behind the bier) 2 Samuel 3:31-35 narrates, which stays sourced to the text itself. Separately checked for coverage of diplomatic/political feast-hosting protocol (courtyard vs. hall, seating, vessels) relevant to claim-feast-form: the book's 'meals' content sits within its household/family chapter (ordinary household food production and consumption), and no page-level discussion of state or covenant-meal hosting architecture was found — this claim stays design-placeholder/speculative and king-stager-2001 is not added to its sourceIds, the same 'checked and doesn't cover it' outcome already recorded on this card for claim-anointing-rite-form at M4.
